title: Numeric Data Types
description: Master SMALLINT, INTEGER, BIGINT, NUMERIC/DECIMAL, REAL, and DOUBLE PRECISION for scientific and financial accuracy.

data.text: Choosing the appropriate numeric type affects both physical storage footprint and calculation precision. PostgreSQL offers integer types for counting, arbitrary-precision decimals for currency, and floating-point types for scientific computation.

rows: Small enum codes, status flags, days of week
Large table primary keys, financial micro-units
Up to 131,072 digits before decimal; 16,383 digits after
Financial balances, money, invoices (zero rounding error)
Scientific measurements where rounding is acceptable

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always use `NUMERIC / DECIMAL` for currency to prevent floating point drift.
Use `BIGINT` for auto-incrementing primary keys on high-velocity tables.
Use `SMALLINT` for constrained lookup values to save cache memory.
